slot.brief: Ice at 0°C mixed with water at a higher temperature; use latent heat plus specific heat to find the final temperature (or remaining ice).

stem: A $50$ g piece of ice at $0^\circ$C is added to $200$ g of water at $40^\circ$C. Find the final temperature. Take the specific heat capacity of water as $1\ \text{cal g}^{-1}\, ^\circ\text{C}^{-1}$ and the latent heat of fusion of ice as $80\ \text{cal g}^{-1}$.

verdicts.working: Water releases 200×40 = 8000 cal cooling to 0°C. Melting the ice takes 50×80 = 4000 cal; the remaining 4000 cal warms 250 g of water, giving T = 4000/(250×1) = 16°C.

working:
$200(40-T)=50(80)+50T$

Independent check: Water releases 200×40 = 8000 cal cooling to 0°C. Melting the ice takes 50×80 = 4000 cal; the remaining 4000 cal warms 250 g of water, giving T = 4000/(250×1) = 16°C.
solution:
Heat lost by the water equals the heat needed to melt the ice and warm the melted ice to $T$.
$$200(40-T)=50(80)+50T$$
Solving gives $T=16^\circ$C.
